body.x: Seomjae (CEO Da-Gyeom Jang) attended 'CES Unveiled,' a global media event held on January 5th (local time) before CES 2025.

Seomjae is an EdTech company aspiring to innovate education globally by merging education and technology (Contech). Starting as an educational content production company in 2017, Seomjae has focused on developing AI-based technologies since 2023, aiming to provide personalized learning solutions powered by data.

Highlighting its focus on providing student-centered, personalized learning experiences through the convergence of AI and content, Seomjae explained its commitment to overcoming the limitations of traditional instructor-centered learning methods. It aims to deliver education tailored to each student’s learning style, preferences, and goals. The company emphasized that its latest product, 'CHALK 3.0,' utilizes Ontolos, an ontology-based AI operating system, to maximize student learning outcomes. This system enhances learning efficiency by designing personalized roadmaps, offering real-time feedback, and employing a gamified learning management system (G-LMS) to boost motivation.

Having successfully introduced premium services in the Korean market, Seomjae has also achieved notable outcomes globally. In 2024, its closed beta test of CHALK 3.0 in Seoul and Boston completed a 76.4% course completion rate. The platform has garnered international recognition for its technological excellence, winning consecutive innovation awards in the EdTech category at CES. Additionally, through collaboration with the MIT CSAIL Alliance, Seomjae is advancing its AI technologies and systems using global learning data.

At CES, Seomjae plans to introduce CHALK 3.0 to the global market and establish new partnerships. According to the company, the third-generation CHALK is a personalized learning platform that analyzes students’ learning goals and current progress to provide tailored learning roadmaps. It even considers learning preferences to guide students on the shortest path to achieving their goals.

CHALK 3.0's AI tutoring function solves problems students encounter during learning in real-time. The learning outcomes are visualized on a dashboard, allowing learners to track their progress immediately. The platform offers real-time AI feedback, Q&A features, step-by-step explanations, and supplementary materials. It supports voice and text input, enabling students to interact in their preferred style.

body.cap: At the CES Unveiled event, Seomjae representatives presented their platform to Aving News reporter Jay Kennedy Marcus. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Through an on-demand content creation system, Seomjae provides content tailored to users’ preferences and needs based on data. The gamified G-LMS feature motivates learners and enhances learning sustainability by visually representing achievements. Students can earn points based on their progress, exchange them for virtual rewards, and expand their learning network by comparing or collaborating with peers.
A comprehensive dashboard allows parents and students to monitor learning progress, strengths, and weaknesses in real-time.

Ontolos, known for its accuracy and flexibility, supports all these features. Seomjae’s AI engine, Ontolos, processes data based on ontology to understand learners’ contexts and provide appropriate solutions. The company emphasized that it overcomes the limitations of conventional GPT-based AI and sets a new standard for personalized learning and content creation.

The platform designs optimized learning roadmaps for individual students and offers higher accuracy than general large language models (LLMs). It also addresses the hallucination problem common in AI models, ensuring reliable answers for learners.

body.x: The company stated, "We plan to expand into the U.S. market, building on our foundation in Korea. We are signing MOUs with offline operators in Boston and will continue partnerships on the West Coast in 2025. Our primary goal in participating in CES is to recruit technology and education partners in the U.S. market."

Seomjae added, "Through partnerships, we will strengthen our market competitiveness with localized content, curricula, and distribution networks. Ultimately, we aim to become a global education navigation system that proposes optimal learning methods and paths tailored to individuals and nurtures talents aligned with the spirit of the times."

Seomjae participated in CES 2025 as part of the startup-focused exhibition area of the Seoul Pavilion in Eureka Park. The Seoul Pavilion, expanded by over 50% from the previous year to 1,040 square meters, features 104 startups. It represents a collaboration between three Seoul districts (Gangnam, Geumcheon, and Gwanak), five startup support organizations (SBA, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, and Campus Town Growth Center), and eight universities (Konkuk, Kyung Hee, Kookmin, Dongguk, Sogang, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Yonsei, and Chung-Ang).
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
